A Scatter Library over Patient Shape

Scatter is the x rays a patient deflects onto the detector: it adds a low, smooth signal under every projection and, uncorrected, cups and streaks the image. BasisSimulator models it today with one analytic convolution, a single 50 mm Gaussian scaled by a single patient diameter, with no anti-scatter grid, no collimation width and no scatter spectrum.

This notebook builds what replaces it: a library of pencil-beam scatter kernels, simulated in Geant4, in water elliptical cylinders from 14 to 50 cm thick in 2 cm steps and from 0.6 to 2.5 times as wide as thick, for every ray through them and every photon energy, scored at once on the detectors of six scanners (with their own grids and efficiencies, from notebooks 03–08). A scan stands each view of the patient in the water ellipse that matches it, ray by ray: thick and narrow from the side, thin and wide from the front. The library keeps apart the scatter last sent by a Compton and by a Rayleigh scattering (and, of the Rayleigh, what it turned by less than 10°), and how far the detected photons travelled at each energy, so a patient that is not water (solid water, bone, iodine) has each part scaled by what its own materials make.

DukeSim reruns its Monte Carlo through every patient; this library is computed once and serves any patient in seconds, primary by ray tracing and scatter from the kernels, and keeps the energy of every scattered photon, which a photon-counting detector needs. It is version 2: version 1 stood every ray in a water cylinder of the patient's water-equivalent diameter, and was 12–19 % off at the centre of non-round patients (notebook 11).

Every claim here is checked: the notebook ends with a scorecard of quantitative pass/fail checks (the library's own noise, symmetry, forced detection against counting photon by photon, held-out thicknesses, aspects and energies, version 1 where the two overlap, and the library against direct Monte Carlo of whole fan beams through round and non-round patients), saved with the library.

How One Kernel Serves Every Scanner

A ray along the thickness of an elliptical cylinder crosses it along a path fixed by its offset from the axis, the impact: a fraction of the ellipse's half-width as that ray sees it, so that 1 grazes the edge whatever the shape (a ray tilted toward the side, as the rays of a fan are, sees an ellipse that is wider than thick as a little narrower, and one thicker than wide as a little wider). So the Monte Carlo fires one ray at an impact through a water ellipse and logs every photon that leaves it, where and in which direction. Outside the patient a photon travels in a straight line, so for each scanner the focal spot is put back on the ray's line, at that scanner's source-to-isocentre distance, and every photon is followed to that scanner's detector arc, through its anti-scatter grid, into its detector. One simulation, six scanners.

A scan puts each kernel under its own ray, moved across the fan by the ray's angle from the kernel's. The detector's columns are 2° wide, and the scatter of a ray near a patient's edge is mostly a sharp forward peak at the ray itself: moved by part of a column and shared between two, that peak would smear across the steepest part of the scan. So the kernels also keep where in each column their scatter landed (its mean and spread), and a column is moved as what it holds: a peak lands whole, scatter spread over its column is shared as before.

A kernel's ray is surrounded by water as its ellipse places it; a patient's is not. A thorax is dense in the middle (the mediastinum and the spine) and light at the sides (the lungs): the scatter a ray beside the mediastinum sends toward the middle is stopped there, and what it sends out through a lung escapes. The scatter of a ray's first scattering, most of what a grid lets through near the ray, can be computed in any medium (a quadrature of what forced detection integrates along a kernel's ray, with Geant4's angular distributions of water). So a scan has each kernel give up its own single scatter, computed in its water ellipse, for the ray's own, computed in the patient as its rays describe it (each ray's water spread evenly along its length through the outline), and keeps the kernel's multiple scatter. For a patient that is its own water ellipse the two are the same.

Counting Scatter by Forced Detection

Counting only the photons that happen to land on a detector wastes nearly all of them: of a million photons along one ray through 45 cm of water, about fifty end up detected as scatter behind a 2-D anti-scatter grid. So the library scores every Compton and Rayleigh scattering Geant4 makes with the chance that the photon's next flight reaches each detector: the scattering's angular distribution (from Geant4's own scattering functions and form factors for hydrogen and oxygen), the attenuation of the water on the way out (exact, in a cylinder), the grid and the detector. Geant4 still follows every photon to its end, so all the multiple scattering is there. The first scattering of each photon along the ray is not even sampled: its chance per millimetre of depth is known, so it is integrated over the ray.

Rayleigh scattering's narrow forward cone is found by also drawing directions from the cone itself, combined with points spread over the detector by multiple importance sampling; scatterings that can add little (deep, with every way out long) are played by Russian roulette. None of this biases the result, and it is checked: every kernel also carries the photon-by-photon count of the same scatter, and the two are compared over the whole library in the scorecard. Section 2 shows one kernel counted both ways.

note! (generic function with 1 method)
"""
An in-figure annotation on a translucent rounded background, so it never fights the data.
"""
function note!(
        ax,
        x,
        y,
        text;
        align = (:left, :center),
        color = PALETTE.ink,
        fontsize = 16,
        offset = (0, 0),
        alpha = 0.85,
    )
    return Mke.textlabel!(
        ax,
        Mke.Point2f(x, y);
        text,
        text_align = align,
        text_color = color,
        fontsize,
        offset,
        background_color = (:white, alpha),
        strokewidth = 0,
        padding = (7, 7, 4, 4),
        cornerradius = 5,
    )
end

# For scatter only the photons matter: electrons stop within a millimetre of where they are made,
# so they are not followed further than that, which makes a patient several times quicker to cross
physics = MC.PhysicsSettings(; production_cut_um = 1000.0, electron_step_um = 1000.0)

1. The Six Detectors

Each scanner as notebooks 03–08 built it: its source-to-isocentre and source-to-detector distances, fan, coverage along z, anti-scatter grid (2-D on the Force, NAEOTOM Alpha, Revolution Apex and Brilliance iCT; 1-D on the Definition Flash and Aquilion ONE), and its detector's efficiency at every energy, read from the tables those notebooks saved. A photon arriving at an angle to the grid's focused walls gets through with probability 1 − H tan α / opening in each direction the grid has walls; a photon crossing the crystal obliquely has a longer path in it. The tally's bins are 2° across the fan and 10–20 mm along z, covering the detector's full width on either side of a ray.

    gemstone = MC.DetectorMaterial(
        "Gemstone 6.40";

            "Al" => 0.163,
            "O" => 0.231,
            "Ce" => 0.002,

# Forced detection on all six detectors, the first scatterings integrated along each ray
readout = MC.ForcedScatterReadout(
    scanners;
    water_mu_per_mm = water_mu,
    water_compton_per_mm = water_compton,
    water_rayleigh_per_mm = water_rayleigh,
)

2. The Kernels

Water ellipses from 14 to 50 cm thick in 2 cm steps, each 0.6, 0.8, 1, 1.25, 1.6, 2 and 2.5 times as wide as thick (but never more than 70 cm wide: the grid's widest corners are no one's, and are made 70 cm wide); rays at 21 impacts from the axis to the edge (0 to 0.95 of the half-width in steps of 0.05, and 0.99); photons of 20 to 140 keV in 10 keV steps: 36,309 kernels. The steps were chosen from version 1's finer grid: dropping every other 1 cm diameter and interpolating it back errs by at most 1.9 %, while 0.1 steps in impact (up to 17 %) and 20 keV steps in energy (up to 60 %, across the detectors' K-edges) do not, and are kept at 0.05 and 10 keV. A larger patient lets less through, so the photons per kernel grow with its area. Each kernel is simulated in two independent halves with their own seeds: the library is their sum, and the difference between the halves measures the library's noise (section 3).

One kernel, counted both ways. A ray at 0.3 of the radius through 35 cm of water, 70 keV, 200,000 photons: the scatter on two detectors across the fan (summed along z), counted photon by photon and by forced detection, from the very same photons.

photons_per_half (generic function with 1 method)
# Photons per kernel in each of its two halves: more for a larger patient, which lets less through
# (by its area, through the diameter of the circle of the same area)
photons_per_half(T, r) = 10_000 * cld(round(Int, 0.5 * 250_000 * (2 * MC.kernel_half_width(T, r) * T / 350^2)), 10_000)
kernel_seed (generic function with 2 methods)
# Each kernel half's own seed, from its ellipse, ray and half
kernel_seed(T, r, u, half = 1) = 200_000 + round(Int, 1000 * T + 100_000_000 * r + 100 * u) + 1_000_000_000 * (half - 1)

    physics,
    readout,

)

# Geant4's attenuation of water at every keV, in all and by Compton and Rayleigh scattering: the
# primary of any ray is then Beer–Lambert, exact, and so is forced detection's way out of the patient
water_mu, water_compton, water_rayleigh = [
    [MC.geant4_attenuation(MC.DetectorMaterial(:Water), Float64(E); kind) for E in 1:150]

library_halves = [
    MC.shape_scatter_library(
            kernel_halves[half:2:end],
            scanners,
            thicknesses_mm,
            aspects,

How the scatter one ray sends to each detector grows with the patient: through the axis (impact 0) of cylinders from 20 to 50 cm, at 70 keV. The 2-D grids (Force, Alpha, Apex, iCT) let through a fraction of what the 1-D grids (Flash, Aquilion ONE) do.

3. The Checks

Six kinds, each a number with a target:

  • The library's noise. Each kernel's two halves are independent estimates; half their difference is the noise of their sum. It is measured where the library is used: on single rays of a 120 kV beam (each ray's kernels over the beam's energies) and on whole scans predicted from each half of the library.

  • Symmetry. A ray through the axis scatters equally to both sides of the fan: summed over every thickness, aspect and energy, the two sides must agree to well within what noise allows.

  • Forced detection against counting. Over every kernel, the scatter by forced detection and the scatter counted photon by photon, from the same photons, must agree.

  • Held-out thicknesses, aspects and energies. Kernels simulated between the library's grid points (23, 33 and 45 cm thick; 0.7, 1.1, 1.4 and 2.2 times as wide; 75 keV), each with eight times the library's photons, must match the library's interpolation.

  • Version 1, where they overlap. At aspect 1 the ellipses are version 1's cylinders: the two libraries, built from independent photons, must agree there within their noise.

  • Whole scans. A fan beam from a 120 kV tube through two cylinders (27.5 and 43.5 cm) and two ellipses (38 × 27 cm, wide and thin; 26 × 35 cm, tall and narrow), all between the grid's points, is simulated directly, every photon, and its scatter on the Force's and the Aquilion ONE's detectors compared with the library's prediction from its pencil kernels: at the centre, across the fan and along z.

noise_cases = [(T, r, u) for T in (200.0, 340.0, 500.0) for r in (0.6, 1.0, 1.6) for u in (0.0, 0.5, 0.9)]
kernel_difference (generic function with 1 method)
"""Relative difference of two kernels: of their totals, and rms over the bins above 10 % of the peak."""
function kernel_difference(a, b)
    total = abs(sum(a) / sum(b) - 1)
    strong = findall(>(0.1 * maximum(b)), b)
    bins = sqrt(sum(abs2, a[strong] ./ b[strong] .- 1) / length(strong))
    return (total = total, bins = bins)
end
beam_kernel (generic function with 1 method)
"""The kernel of one ray of the 120 kV beam: each energy's kernel, weighted by the beam's photons."""
function beam_kernel(lib, name, T, r, u)
    energies, weights = scan_spectrum
    kernel = zero(MC.library_kernel(lib, name, T, r, u, 70.0)[1])
    for (E, w) in zip(energies, weights)
        w > 0 || continue
        kernel .+= w / sum(weights) .* MC.library_kernel(lib, name, T, r, u, E)[1]
    end
    return kernel
end

# The noise of each ray's kernel: half the difference of the library's two halves
noise_differences = [
    let a = beam_kernel(library_halves[1], s.name, case...),
            b = beam_kernel(library_halves[2], s.name, case...),
            d = kernel_difference(a, b)
            (total = d.total / 2, bins = d.bins / 2)
    end
        for case in noise_cases for s in scanners
]

energy_noise = [
    (
            scanner = s.name,
            D = T,
            E = E,
            total = kernel_difference(
                MC.library_kernel(library_halves[1], s.name, T, 1.0, 0.0, E)[1],
                MC.library_kernel(library_halves[2], s.name, T, 1.0, 0.0, E)[1],
            ).total / 2,
        )
        for T in (400.0, 460.0, 500.0) for E in (50.0, 70.0, 90.0) for s in scanners
]

The noise of single energies. One ray at one energy through the axis of the largest patients is the noisiest kernel in the library: at worst 9.3 % in its total (SOMATOM Force, 50.0 cm, 50 keV), and up to 3.5 % at 70 keV. Almost all of it is multiple scattering, photons that diffused through 40–50 cm of water before reaching the detector, which forced detection cannot make less rare. No scan uses such a kernel alone: each ray carries the beam's whole spectrum and each scan hundreds of rays, so the checks judge the noise there.

# Each held-out kernel from eight independent runs, each with the library's photons per kernel
held_out_runs = let
    runs = MC.simulate_sweep(
        [
            (
                    MC.kernel_phantom(T, r),
                    E,
                    kernel_seed(T, r, u) + 11 + 1000 * chunk,
                    MC.kernel_ray(T, r, u),
                    2 * photons_per_half(T, r),
                )
                for (T, r, u, E) in held_out_cases for chunk in 1:8
        ];
        physics,
        readout,
    )
    [MC.merge_tallies(runs[(8j - 7):(8j)]) for j in eachindex(held_out_cases)]
end

# The kernels' Monte Carlo primaries against Beer–Lambert, where enough primaries got through to
# measure them to 1 % (at least ten thousand, so that 5 % is five times their noise): a check of
# the transport and of the scoring together
primary_differences = let
    s = scanners[1]
    cases = [(T, u, E) for T in (140.0, 200.0, 300.0) for u in (0.0, 0.5, 0.9, 0.95) for E in (60.0, 80.0, 100.0, 120.0)]
    differences = Float64[]
    for (T, u, E) in cases
        iT, ir, iu, iE = findfirst(==(T), thicknesses_mm), findfirst(==(1.0), aspects), findfirst(==(u), impact_fractions), findfirst(==(E), energies_keV)
        chord = T * sqrt(1 - u^2)
        k = round(Int, E)
        transmission = exp(-water_mu[k] * chord)
        transmission * 2 * photons_per_half(T, 1.0) >= 10_000 || continue
        expected = transmission * s.efficiency[k] * E
        push!(differences, abs(library.primary[s.name][iu, ir, iT, iE] / expected - 1))
    end
    differences
end

# Rays through the axis: the scatter on the two halves of the fan, summed over every thickness, aspect
# and energy (each kernel then counts by its signal, the precise ones most)
symmetry = [
    let sides = [
                let kernel = MC.library_kernel(library, s.name, T, r, 0.0, E)[1]
                    half = size(kernel, 1) ÷ 2
                    (sum(kernel[1:half, :]), sum(kernel[(end - half + 1):end, :]))
            end
                for T in thicknesses_mm for r in aspects for E in energies_keV
            ]
            abs(log(sum(first, sides) / sum(last, sides)))
    end
        for s in scanners
]

# Forced detection against the photon-by-photon count of the same photons: each scanner's total over
# every kernel, for the patients up to 34 cm thick and those above
forced_vs_analog = [
    let kernels = [j for (j, (T, r, u, E)) in enumerate(kernel_grid) if (T <= 340) == small]
            forced = sum(sum(kernel_tallies[j][k].scatter) / kernel_tallies[j][k].n for j in kernels)
            analog = sum(sum(kernel_tallies[j][k].analog_scatter) / kernel_tallies[j][k].n for j in kernels)
            (scanner = s.name, sizes = small ? "14–34 cm" : "36–50 cm", difference = abs(forced / analog - 1))
    end
        for (k, s) in enumerate(scanners) for small in (true, false)
]

# Version 1, where the two libraries overlap: the cylinders (aspect 1) at every thickness of version 2
# within version 1's diameters, on rays of the 120 kV beam at five impacts; nothing if version 1's file is not here
regression = let
    path = joinpath(table_dir, "scatter_library_geant4.jls")
    if isfile(path)
        previous = Serialization.deserialize(path)
        energies, weights = scan_spectrum
        old_beam(name, D, u) = sum(
            w / sum(weights) .* MC.library_kernel(previous, name, D, u, E)[1] for (E, w) in zip(energies, weights) if w > 0
        )
        [
            (scanner = s.name, T = T, u = u, difference = kernel_difference(beam_kernel(library, s.name, T, 1.0, u), old_beam(s.name, T, u)))
                for s in scanners
                for T in thicknesses_mm if first(previous.diameters_mm) <= T <= last(previous.diameters_mm)
                for u in (0.0, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9)
        ]
    else
        nothing
    end
end

Whole scans. The tube: BasisSimulator's IPEM spectrum at 120 kV through 9.2 mm of aluminium (the Aquilion ONE beam fitted in notebook 08), a 40 mm beam at the isocentre, no bowtie. The direct simulation fires the fan beam from the focal spot through the cylinder at the isocentre, 96 million photons per case in 64 independent chunks (whose spread gives its own noise), scored on the one scanner by forced detection. The library sums its pencil kernels for rays every 0.1° across the fan, each weighted by its share of the beam's photons and energies. Each kernel reaches a full detector width on either side of its own row, so along z the library covers whole the rows within that reach of every ray in the beam (complete_rows): the whole detector and more, where the two are compared.

scan_spectrum = let
    scanner = BS.EICTScanner(
        source_to_isocenter = 600.0,
        source_to_detector = 1072.0,
        detector_rows = 320,
        detector_cols = 896,
        detector_row_size = 0.5,
        detector_col_size = 0.5756,
        detector_shape = :arc,
        target_angle = 10.0,
        flat_filter_material = :aluminum,
        flat_filter_thickness = 9.2,
        bowtie_filter = :large_body,
        detector_material = :ufc,
        detector_depth = 1.4,
    )
    protocol = BS.CTProtocol(;
        kVp = 120,
        mA = 200.0,
        views = 1200,
        rotation_time = 0.5,
        collimation_mm = 40.0,
    )
    BS.resolve_source_spectrum_without_bowtie(BS.SimOptions(), protocol; scanner)
end

# Every photon of the fan beam, 64 independent chunks of 1.5 million per case
direct_scans = [
    let s = scanners[findfirst(x -> x.name == case.name, scanners)]
            phantom = MC.CylinderPhantom(;
                semi_axes_mm = case.semi_axes_mm,
                centre_mm = (0.0, s.source_to_isocenter_mm),
            )
            beam = MC.FocalSpot(;
                distance_mm = s.source_to_isocenter_mm,
                fan_deg = s.fan_deg,
                z_half_mm = 20.0,
            )
            chunks = MC.simulate_sweep(
                [(phantom, MC.Spectrum(scan_spectrum...), 500 + chunk, beam) for chunk in 1:64];
                n = 1_500_000,
                physics,
                readout = MC.ForcedScatterReadout([s]; water_mu_per_mm = water_mu),
            )
            (all = only(MC.merge_tallies(chunks)), chunks = [only(c) for c in chunks])
    end
        for case in scan_cases
]

# The library's prediction from rays every 0.1° across the fan, each crossing its chord of the
# patient; from the whole library and from each of its halves, and the rows every ray's kernel
# reaches whole
library_scans = [
    let s = scanners[findfirst(x -> x.name == case.name, scanners)]
            cols = MC.column_edges(s)
            centre = (0.0, s.source_to_isocenter_mm)
            rays = [
                (
                    angle_deg = γ,
                    wet_mm = MC.ellipse_chord((0.0, 0.0), (sind(γ), cosd(γ)), centre, case.semi_axes_mm),
                    weight = abs(γ) <= s.fan_deg / 2 ? 0.1 / s.fan_deg : 0.0,
                )
                for γ in (cols[1] + 0.05):0.1:cols[end]
            ]
            predict(lib) = MC.library_scan(lib, s.name, rays; collimation_mm = 40.0, spectrum = scan_spectrum)
            whole = predict(library)
            (
                all = whole.scatter,
                halves = [predict(half).scatter for half in library_halves],
                complete = whole.complete_rows,
            )
    end
        for case in scan_cases
]

# The direct simulation against the library, per photon: at the centre (the three middle columns
# of the beam's rows), across the fan (each column, summed over the beam's rows) and along z (each
# row the library covers whole, summed over the columns the patient covers); and the noise of both
scan_differences = [
    let t = direct_scans[j].all
            direct = t.scatter ./ t.n
            predicted = library_scans[j].all
            halves = library_scans[j].halves
            rows = (t.row_edges_mm[1:(end - 1)] .+ t.row_edges_mm[2:end]) ./ 2
            s = scanners[findfirst(x -> x.name == case.name, scanners)]
            beam = findall(z -> abs(z) < 20.0 * s.source_to_detector_mm / s.source_to_isocenter_mm, rows)
            c = (size(direct, 1) + 1) ÷ 2
            middle = (c - 1):(c + 1)
            centre(m) = sum(m[middle, beam])
            across(m) = vec(sum(m[:, beam]; dims = 2))
            inside = findall(>(0.2 * maximum(across(direct))), across(direct))
            along(m) = vec(sum(m[inside, :]; dims = 1))
            profile = along(direct)
            covered = findall(
                r -> library_scans[j].complete[r] && profile[r] > 0.05 * maximum(profile),
                eachindex(profile),
            )
            rms(a, b) = sqrt(sum(abs2, a ./ b .- 1) / length(a))
            chunk_centres = [centre(k.scatter ./ k.n) for k in direct_scans[j].chunks]
            (
                centre = abs(centre(predicted) / centre(direct) - 1),
                across = rms(across(predicted)[inside], across(direct)[inside]),
                along = rms(along(predicted)[covered], along(direct)[covered]),
                library_noise_centre = abs(centre(halves[1]) / centre(halves[2]) - 1) / 2,
                library_noise_across = rms(across(halves[1])[inside], across(halves[2])[inside]) / 2,
                direct_noise_centre = std(chunk_centres) / sqrt(length(chunk_centres)) / mean(chunk_centres),
            )
    end
        for (j, case) in enumerate(scan_cases)
]

Saving the Library

Three files in lib/BasisMonteCarlo/tables/, all made here:

  • scatter_library_v2.toml and scatter_library_v2.bin: what BasisSimulator reads, with nothing of BasisMonteCarlo. The binary file is the arrays, little-endian Float32 in Julia's column-major order, one after another: for each scanner its scatter and rayleigh kernels (column, row, impact, aspect, thickness, energy) and its primary (impact, aspect, thickness, energy), per incident photon. The TOML header gives each array's shape and byte offset, the axes and their values, each scanner's geometry and bins, Geant4's attenuation of water on a 1-keV grid, how the library was made and the scorecard above. read_scatter_library reads it with Base and TOML alone; BasisSimulator keeps its own copy of that reader.

  • scatter_library_v2.jls: the same library as BasisMonteCarlo's type, for notebook 11.

saved = let
    path = joinpath(table_dir, "scatter_library_v2")
    library.metadata["scorecard"] = MC.scorecard(checks)
    library.metadata["checks_passed"] = count(c -> c.passed, checks)
    library.metadata["checks_total"] = length(checks)
    Serialization.serialize(path * ".jls", library)
    MC.write_scatter_library(
        path,
        library;
        scorecard = MC.scorecard(checks),
        provenance = Dict{String, Any}(
            "source" => "BasisMonteCarlo.jl (Geant4 via Geant4.jl), notebook 10_scatter_library.jl",
            "physics" => string(physics),
            "checks" => "$(count(c -> c.passed, checks)) of $(length(checks)) pass",
        ),
    )
    path
end;
